title: Mayor's draft 2026 budget presentation day
subtitle: Reserves, development charge shortfall, service reductions, utility rates, debt strategy, transit, parks and next steps in budget process
overview: Council spent the day hearing staff present the Mayor's draft 2026 budget update, the second confirmation year of the 2024 to 2027 cycle. The draft proposes a city services tax levy increase of about 3.15 per cent, down from the 4.51 per cent forecast, with a separate hospital levy of 0.21 per cent. Local boards and shared services budgets come later and will add to the total.

Staff said slower growth, lower development charge collections, inflation and tariffs drove the changes. To hold the increase down, the draft includes service reductions such as ending winter maintenance of on-street bike lanes, 24/7 paid parking in city lots, a higher mixed-waste drop-off fee and cuts to some parks and culture programming. It also funds the South End Community Centre, two paramedic shifts, and permanent seniors and youth ride-free transit.

Council also referred a set of companion-report recommendations to the November 26 budget meeting. They cover reserve rebuilding, inter-reserve borrowing, the debt strategy and parking and building maintenance reviews. No final decisions were made. The mayor plans to sign off on the final budget between November 10 and 13, with public delegations on November 18. After a closed session, the mayor reported that council received information and gave no direction.

decisions.detail: Recommendations going to the November 26 meeting direct staff to rebuild below-target tax-supported contingency reserves as a first priority from year-end surpluses, up to at least 75 per cent of target, and to assess funding in the 2028 to 2031 cycle.
Recommended that council approve the debt strategy in the 2026 update and acknowledge the projected debt burden may affect the City's future credit rating.
Recommended approval of inter-reserve fund borrowing in 2026, including to keep the Ontario Building Code Stabilization reserve fund in balance after the 2025 deficit projection.
Recommended replacing $49,207,200 of debt financing for the FM Woods Station Upgrade with funding from the Water Capital reserve fund.
Recommended readopting the 2026-2027 rates, fees and charges, subject to amendments in the 2027 confirmation year, and approving 2026 reserve transfers.
Recommended directing staff to analyse the downtown parking operating model within the City-Wide Parking Study and review corporate building maintenance budgets, both for the 2027 budget update.

debate: Councillors questioned the development charge forecast, with one noting the later-year projections looked high against the recent trend. Staff said 2026 and 2027 were revised down, while later years remain tied to the 2023 background study and will be revisited annually.

Several councillors asked about the cuts. Parks staff said the park stewardship program involves hundreds of volunteers and is wrapping up. Staff said tree bylaw enforcement without added funding would be education-focused and slower, and bike lane winter maintenance would end under the draft.

One councillor challenged the removal of climate-related capital funding, the 100 per cent renewable energy account, asking whether it abandons the net zero goal. Staff said the pace is slowing, not the goal, and pointed to transit and fleet electrification and a plan coming in early 2026.

On parks, a councillor pressed on delays to a neighbourhood park and a splash pad project. Staff recommended keeping the splash pad, washrooms and other elements as one bundled project to avoid higher costs and longer closures, and said unresolved encroachment issues will go to council in 2026.

Councillors asked whether new rec centre and library costs could be phased in. Staff said staffing is already phased into 2027 and 2026 reflects only the part-year need. They also said debt issuance funds long-lived assets and is not the same as being in net debt.
